statement: In 12 healthy volunteers who had used MDA, or both MDMA and a classic psychedelic, before, one dose of MDA by mouth in hospital (1.4 mg/kg, 83 to 128 mg; study condition), compared not with MDMA in the same people but with MDMA data (1.5 mg/kg; study condition) from other volunteers in two earlier studies by the same team, whose self-ratings and heart rate were recorded for 6 hours instead of the 8 recorded after MDA, was associated with effects that lasted longer, more visual and 'spiritual' effects, fewer anxious ones and a smaller rise in heart rate (Baggott et al., 2019). Because this comparison is across separate studies and not randomized, and the MDMA volunteers are not described (16 in some analyses, 12 in others), any of these differences may come from who was studied or how long they were watched rather than from the drugs. Length: at 6 hours no MDMA rating was still significantly above its dummy pill, whereas all five general drug-effect ratings still were after MDA (any drug effect 46.4 points above its dummy pill on a 0 to 100 scale, and 41.6 points above MDMA, at that hour); at 8 hours all but the bad-effect rating were still raised after MDA, a time at which MDMA was not recorded. Kind: on a 66-item altered-states questionnaire rated at 8 hours for the peak of the experience (12 people per drug), MDA was rated higher than MDMA on complex and elementary visual imagery and on spiritual experience, and only MDA raised 'audio-visual synesthesia' (sounds changing what is seen); MDMA was rated higher than MDA on anxiety, 'dread of ego dissolution' and impaired control and thinking, three scales on which MDA did not differ from its dummy pill; both drugs raised blissful state, 'oceanic boundlessness', visionary changes, insightfulness, a sense of unity, changed meaning of things perceived and feeling out of the body. Against its dummy pill MDA raised ratings of feeling close to others, as MDMA did against its own (the two did not differ significantly), while on a scale of social feelings only MDMA raised warmth toward others ('Affiliation'; no statistic printed). The authors' description of MDA as more inward and emotionally intense, and of MDMA as more outgoing, is their impression, without data. Heart and blood pressure: heart rate rose by 20 (± 3) beats a minute after MDA against 30.6 (± 4.5) after MDMA (p = 0.03), although the abstract and discussion call the rises similar; MDA's highest reading came from 8 hourly measurements and MDMA's from 6, and a longer window can only raise a maximum, so the window does not explain MDA's smaller rise (editors' reasoning); the highest systolic pressure rose by 33 and 31 mmHg and diastolic by 24 and 19 mmHg (difference p = 0.06). Unwanted effects: over the whole session, ratings of a bad drug effect were not significantly above either dummy pill (at 6 hours MDA's was), and ratings of feeling anxious or paranoid showed no significant effect of condition; the abstract calls MDA well tolerated, but the paper reports no adverse events at all, although its methods describe safety monitoring and a check two weeks later. MDA's half-life in blood averaged 10.9 hours (SD 4); the paper compares it with MDMA figures from another team's study, and its abstract and discussion disagree on whether the half-life explains the longer effects. The volunteers were screened, healthy and experienced, few of them women (number not given), in hospital, given one known dose each; MDA and its dummy pill came on consecutive days, with MDA still in the blood on the second day in the half who had the dummy pill second; nobody took a second dose, so taking more was not studied; people with heart disease were excluded, and the authors say the blood-pressure rises could matter for them. The paper did not ask why MDMA is more widely used than MDA. Its authors write, citing other papers, that MDA is often sold as 'ecstasy' in place of MDMA. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: How is MDA different from MDMA? Only one lab study has compared them, and not in the same people. Twelve healthy volunteers who had used such drugs before took MDA and, on another day, a dummy pill in hospital, without knowing which; their results were set beside MDMA results from other people in the same team's earlier studies, who were watched for 6 hours instead of 8. MDA's effects seemed to last longer: they were still clearly there at 8 hours, while MDMA's had faded by 6. MDA brought more visions with eyes closed and more 'spiritual' feelings, and less anxiety and loss of control, than MDMA did; both made people feel close to others. Heart rate rose by about 20 beats a minute after MDA, against about 31 after MDMA, and top blood pressure by about 30 points with both. The paper calls MDA well tolerated but reports no side effects at all. Because the two drugs were tested on different people, watched for different times, these differences may not come from the drugs. Nobody took a second dose, and the study did not ask why MDMA is more popular.
population: 12 healthy, screened adult volunteers with earlier self-reported experience of MDA, or of both MDMA and a classic psychedelic such as LSD, and no drug dependence other than nicotine or caffeine (mean age 27.8, SD 8; few women, number not given), studied during one hospital stay in San Francisco; MDMA comparison data from 12 to 16 other volunteers in two earlier studies by the same team, not described in this paper
exposure: One oral dose of racemic MDA, 1.4 mg/kg (83 to 128 mg), in a capsule after a two-hour fast, given double-blind by researchers in hospital (study conditions)
comparator: Placebo in the same 12 people on the day before or after (half in each order; how the order was set is not stated); for the drug comparison, racemic MDMA 1.5 mg/kg and its placebo given to other volunteers in two earlier studies by the same team (not randomized against MDA; self-ratings and heart rate recorded to 6 hours instead of 8)
outcome: Self-rated drug effects over time (visual analogue scales, to 8 hours after MDA and 6 after MDMA); a 66-item altered-states questionnaire rated at 8 hours for the peak; affect and social-feeling scales before and 2.5 hours after dosing; heart rate and blood pressure hourly; unwanted effects as rated (no adverse-event data reported); MDA's half-life in blood
magnitude: Baggott et al. (2019): MDA n = 12; MDMA comparison n = 16 (visual analogue scales) or 12 (altered-states and affect and social scales). Length: at 6 h no MDMA effect significantly above its placebo; MDA raised all five general drug-effect items at 6 h and all except bad drug effect at 8 h; any drug effect at 6 h 41.6 ± 7 points above MDMA (z = 6.3, p < 0.001) and 46.4 ± 7 above placebo (z = 6.7, p < 0.001); at 8 h 35.6 ± 10 above placebo (t = 3.7, p = 0.001); MDMA not recorded beyond 6 h. Altered-states questionnaire (F(3,21), Westfall-corrected pairwise tests, printed in Figure 1): complex imagery 20.6, elementary imagery 13.9, spiritual experience 24.8 (MDA > MDMA; both > placebo); dread of ego dissolution 15.1, impaired control and cognition 11.1, anxiety 5.09 (p = 0.008) (MDMA > MDA; MDMA > placebo; MDA not > placebo); audio-visual synesthesia 8.26 (MDA > placebo only); oceanic boundlessness 35.9, visionary changes 21.3, blissful state 32.4, insightfulness 19.4, changed meaning of percepts 13.1, experience of unity 17.9, disembodiment 10.8 (both > placebo; no difference between the drugs). Closeness to others (area under the curve, mean ± SEM): MDA 168.0 ± 53 against its placebo 11.5 ± 38; MDMA 114.4 ± 44 against its placebo −12.5 ± 16; MDA and MDMA not significantly different (F(3,21) = 5.26, p = 0.0073). Affiliation raised by MDMA only (no statistic printed). Bad drug effect area 47.9 ± 26 (MDA) and 41.4 ± 16 (MDMA), neither significantly above its placebo (F(3,21) = 3.1, p = 0.0487, no significant pairwise difference); anxious F(3,21) = 1.26, p = 0.3116; paranoia F(3,21) = 1.71, p = 0.196. Heart rate rise 20 ± 3 bpm (MDA) against 30.6 ± 4.5 (MDMA), p = 0.03; peak systolic rise 33 ± 2 against 31 ± 3 mmHg; diastolic 24 ± 2 against 19 ± 2 mmHg, p = 0.06 (the ± is not defined in this paragraph); main effects of condition F(3,22) = 17.1 (heart rate), 61.7 (systolic) and 32.4 (diastolic), p < 0.0001. Prolactin rise 16 ± 6 against 29 ± 6 ng/mL (p = 0.07); cortisol 16 ± 1 against 13 ± 2 µg/dL. MDA half-life 10.9 ± 4 h (mean ± SD); the MDMA half-life compared, 8.1 ± 2 h, is from Kolbrich et al. (2008a; 1.6 mg/kg; another team). No adverse-event data reported. The paper's areas under the curve for any drug effect, high, good drug effect and liking are not used here: they mix strength with length, and the recording windows differed.

risk_of_bias.note: The comparison that carries the claim, MDA against MDMA, is between different people from separate studies, which is why it starts low. On top of that: the unequal recording windows (8 against 6 hours) bear directly on the duration comparison; the MDMA volunteers are not described and their number differs between analyses (16 or 12); MDA and its placebo came on consecutive days with MDA still in the blood the next day; the self-ratings come from experienced volunteers who probably recognised MDA; no registration is reported; computerized tasks, adverse events and the two-week check are not reported (card sc_baggott_2019: RoB 2 high overall; the editors' cross-study domain high). One level, not two, because the heart-rate comparison is objective and the window problem runs against the difference observed (editors' reasoning).

indirectness.note: Rated as worded: one dose of each drug at study doses, in healthy, experienced volunteers in hospital, which the statement says. No comparison of strength is made: the paper's areas under the curve for overall drug effect, high, good effect and liking are not used, because they mix strength with length and the recording windows differed.

imprecision.note: 12 MDA participants and 12 to 16 MDMA participants, no intervals; the heart-rate difference rests on p = 0.03 and the diastolic and prolactin differences on p = 0.06 and 0.07; the differences in kind are F tests in 12 people per drug.

publication_bias.note: Not assessable; no trial registration is reported.

grade.reasoning: The MDA–MDMA comparison is across separate studies and not randomized, so it is rated as observational and starts low (METHODS 6.3; brief for round pdf-2026-11-14), although MDA against its own placebo is a within-person, placebo-controlled comparison. Risk of bias −1 and imprecision −1 give very low (the scale stops there). MDA's effects against its own placebo (raised self-ratings, closeness, perceptual changes, heart rate and blood pressure, effects still present at 8 hours) would be rated higher on their own, but the claim is about how MDA differs from MDMA and inherits its weakest necessary link, the cross-study comparison. Status single study: one paper, whose MDMA data come from the same team's earlier studies (not read). Doses are given only as study conditions and no strength comparison is made. The abstract's 'well-tolerated' has no adverse-event data behind it, which the statement says.
